evidence: Plaut. Rud. 3.4.5: pugnum impingere alicui in ōs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Properly the fist; a punch is given with it: pugnōs in ventrem ingerere (Ter. Phorm. 5.7.95), pugnīs contundere (Plaut.).

terms.gloss: a punch, a cuff, a box on the ear
terms.register: vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.; posteā Quint., Juv.
evidence: Plaut. Pers. 846b: ei, colaphō mē īcit
Ter. Ad. 199: plūs quīngentōs colaphōs īnfrēgit mihi
terms.comment: Greek κόλαφος; the source of Italian colpo and French coup.

phrases.latin: Quae haec rēs est? Ei, colaphō mē īcit.
phrases.english: What’s this? Ow, he’s punched me!

sources: Lewis & Short: pugnus · Lewis & Short: caedo · Lewis & Short: colaphus
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 46, 366.
